attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- new: Start a new project from scratch using the Software Factory process.
- train: Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain.
- launch-check: Pre-launch readiness gate for a built product. Run before going live.
- verdict-30d: 30-day post-launch decision: SCALE, PIVOT, or KILL. No middle ground.
- research: Run competitive intelligence research on any product category or idea.
- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.
- saas-cycle: Full SaaS idea-to-verdict pipeline. Takes an idea from raw concept through build, launch, and mea...
- caveman:compress: Compress natural language memory files (CLAUDE.md, todos, preferences) into caveman format to save input tokens. Preserves all technical substance, code, URLs, and structure. Compressed version overwrites the original file. Human-readable backup saved as FILE.original.md. Trigger: /caveman:compress <filepath> or "compress memory file"
- caveman:caveman-help: Quick-reference card for all caveman modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /caveman-help, "caveman help", "what caveman commands", "how do I use caveman".
- caveman:caveman-review: Ultra-compressed code review comments. Cuts noise from PR feedback while preserving the actionable signal. Each comment is one line: location, problem, fix. Use when user says "review this PR", "code review", "review the diff", "/review", or invokes /caveman-review. Auto-triggers when reviewing pull requests.
- caveman:caveman-commit: Ultra-compressed commit message generator. Cuts noise from commit messages while preserving intent and reasoning. Conventional Commits format. Subject ≤50 chars, body only when "why" isn't obvious. Use when user says "write a commit", "commit message", "generate commit", "/commit", or invokes /caveman-commit. Auto-triggers when staging changes.

Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra, wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.

Goal: Build a complete inventory of every section, component, CSS module, image, font, animation, and constant that the homepage uses. We are comparing this to the original Webflow export to find pixel-perfect mismatches.

Read in full:
- src/app/page.tsx
- src/app/layout.tsx
- src/app/globals.css
- Every file under src/components/home/ (list each, read each .tsx and .module.css)
- src/components/animations/ (list + read)
- src/components/shared/ (only files referenced from the homepage — newsletter-signup, beta-cta, cta-banner)
- src/components/layout/navbar.tsx + navbar.module.css
- src/components/layout/footer.tsx + footer.module.css
- src/components/ui/* — list which UI primitives the homepage tree imports
- src/lib/constants/ — list, read any homepage-related ones
- src/lib/seo/ — read homepage metadata if present
- src/types/ — anything used by homepage
- next.config.ts, tailwind config, postcss, package.json (versions of next, react, tailwind, framer-motion, embla)

For EVERY homepage section component, report:
1. File path (with line numbers for key blocks)
2. Section purpose (hero, featured logos, portfolio carousel, pain points, resolution banner, built-for, benefits, how it works, pricing, comparison, FAQ, etc.)
3. Exact CSS Module values: padding, margin, font-size, font-weight, line-height, color, border-radius, box-shadow, gap, grid-template-columns, max-width, breakpoints used

5. Animations / framer-motion usage

Also report:

- Any TODO/FIXME/console.log/any/ts-ignore in the homepage tree

Goal: Extract the EXACT spec the homepage should match — every section in render order, every CSS value, every image, every interaction. We are using this as the source of truth to fix our Next.js implementation.

input.prompt:
Audit the supporting infrastructure for the Boldteq Next.js homepage in /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Marketing Site/Boldteq.

Goal: Confirm fonts, images, global CSS, and config are correctly set up to support pixel-perfect Webflow conversion. Find any infra-level reason the homepage might not match the original.

Check + report:

1. Fonts
   - List files in public/fonts/ (RoobertPRO weights expected: 300, 400, 500, 700)
   - Read src/app/layout.tsx to see how fonts are declared (next/font/local? @font-face in globals.css?)
   - Read src/app/globals.css — find the @font-face declarations + any global typography
   - Compare the Webflow font loading in boldteq-v1-0.webflow/index.html <head> — does it load a different format/weight set?
   - Verify font-display strategy + fallback stack

2. Images
   - List directory structure under public/images/ (just top-level + webflow subdir counts, not every file)
   - Confirm boldteq-v1-0.webflow/images/ has been copied to public/images/webflow/ — count files in each, flag mismatches
   - Read next.config.ts — confirm remotePatterns allow cdn.prod.website-files.com
   - Check if any homepage images are still pointing to the Webflow CDN vs local

3. Global CSS
   - Read src/app/globals.css in full
   - Compare to boldteq-v1-0.webflow/css/normalize.css and webflow.css — are we resetting box-sizing, body margin, default font, link colors the same way? Note any divergence that would cause baseline visual drift across the whole page

4. Tailwind / shadcn
   - Find the tailwind config (v4 inline in CSS or tailwind.config.ts)
   - Confirm Tailwind preflight is not fighting Webflow-style CSS modules (look for layer ordering, base styles)

5. Layout shell
   - Read src/app/layout.tsx — what wraps every page (navbar, footer, providers, font className, html lang, body class)
   - Are PostHog/Sentry providers wrapping in a way that affects render?
   - Check viewport meta, theme-color, head.tsx if any

6. Package.json
   - Report the exact versions of: next, react, react-dom, tailwindcss, framer-motion, embla-carousel-react, @next/font (or next/font), shadcn deps, lucide-react, any other relevant
   - Flag if any are not the latest stable

7. Build / dev sanity
   - Check next.config.ts for image config, redirects, headers
   - Check for any postcss.config / .browserslistrc

Output a structured markdown report. Flag every issue that could cause visual drift before we even get to per-section bugs. Read-only research, do not modify any files.

# Boldteq Next.js Infrastructure Audit Report

## Executive Summary
The Boldteq Next.js homepage infrastructure is **largely correct** for Webflow conversion. All critical fonts, images, and global CSS are properly set up. However, there are several **configuration and usage patterns** that could cause subtle visual drift if not carefully handled.

---

## 1. FONTS ✅ Correct Setup

### Declared Files & Weights
All four required RoobertPRO weights are present in `/public/fonts/`:
- ✅ RoobertPRO-Light (weight 300) — .woff2, .woff, .ttf, .eot
- ✅ RoobertPRO-Regular (weight 400) — .woff2, .woff, .ttf, .eot
- ✅ RoobertPRO-Medium (weight 500) — .woff2, .woff, .ttf, .eot
- ✅ RoobertPRO-Bold (weight 700) — .woff2, .woff, .ttf, .eot

**Location:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Marketing Site/Boldteq/public/fonts/`

### Next.js Font Loading (`src/app/layout.tsx`)
```typescript
const roobertPro = localFont({
  src: [
    { path: "../../public/fonts/RoobertPRO-Light.woff2", weight: "300", style: "normal" },
    { path: "../../public/fonts/RoobertPRO-Regular.woff2", weight: "400", style: "normal" },
    { path: "../../public/fonts/RoobertPRO-Medium.woff2", weight: "500", style: "normal" },
    { path: "../../public/fonts/RoobertPRO-Bold.woff2", weight: "700", style: "normal" },
  ],
  variable: "--font-roobert",
  display: "swap",
});
```
- ✅ Using `next/font/local` (correct modern approach)
- ✅ `font-display: swap` strategy (same as Webflow)
- ✅ CSS custom property `--font-roobert` applied to `<html>`
- ✅ Only loading `.woff2` (most efficient; fallbacks not needed for modern browsers)

### Webflow Reference (@font-face in `boldteq-v1-0.webflow/css/boldteq-v1-0.webflow.css`)
Webflow declares multiple formats per weight:
```css
@font-face {
  font-family: Roobert PRO;
  src: url('../fonts/RoobertPRO-Regular.woff2') format("woff2"), 
       url('../fonts/RoobertPRO-Regular.eot') format("embedded-opentype"), 
       url('../fonts/RoobertPRO-Regular.woff') format("woff"), 
       url('../fonts/RoobertPRO-Regular.ttf') format("truetype");
  font-weight: 400;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}
```
- Both use `font-display: swap` ✅
- Both define all 4 weights (300, 400, 500, 700) ✅

### Global CSS Application (`src/app/globals.css`)
```css
body {
  font-family: var(--font-roobert), Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 28px;
  font-weight: 400;
  color: #111827;
  -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
  -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale;
}
```
- ✅ Proper fallback stack (Roobert → Arial → sans-serif)
- ✅ Font smoothing applied
- ✅ Matches Webflow defaults (16px base size, 400 weight)

### Potential Issue: Font Loading Priority
- **Observation:** Next.js uses `localFont` which loads only woff2. Webflow HTML has no explicit `<link rel="preload">` for fonts in the head, but uses multi-format `@font-face`. 
- **Risk:** Negligible. WOFF2 is universally supported in modern browsers. No visual drift expected.

---

## 2. IMAGES ✅ Mostly Correct, Minor Addition

public/images/
  ├── icons/
  ├── logos/

boldteq-v1-0.webflow/images/

- Next.js copy: **483 files** (1 extra)

### Image CDN Configuration (`next.config.ts`)

  unoptimized: process.env.NODE_ENV === "development",

```
- ✅ Allows `cdn.prod.website-files.com` (Webflow CDN origin)
- ✅ Allows `cdn.sanity.io` (CMS integration)
- ✅ SVG enabled with security policy

### Image Usage in Homepage
All hero and component images use local `/images/webflow/` paths:

## 3. GLOBAL CSS ✅ Well Integrated, Minor Observations

### `src/app/globals.css` Structure
The file uses Tailwind v4 syntax with custom themes:
```css

@import "tw-animate-css";
@import "shadcn/tailwind.css";
```

### Base Layer Resets
```css
@layer base {
  * {
    @apply border-border outline-ring/50;
  }

  html {
    scroll-behavior: smooth;
  }

  body {
    @apply bg-background text-foreground;
    font-family: var(--font-roobert), Arial, sans-serif;
    font-size: 16px;
    line-height: 28px;
    font-weight: 400;

### Comparison to Webflow
| Aspect | Next.js | Webflow | Status |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Box-sizing | Tailwind default (border-box) | `* { box-sizing: border-box }` in webflow.css | ✅ Same |
| Body margin | Tailwind reset (0) | `body { margin: 0 }` in normalize.css | ✅ Same |
| Body font | `font-family: var(--font-roobert)` | `@font-face` rules | ✅ Same outcome |
| Body font-size | `16px` | `14px` (in webflow.css) | ⚠️ **DIVERGENCE** |
| Line-height | `28px` | `20px` (in webflow.css) | ⚠️ **DIVERGENCE** |
| h2 margin | `margin-top/bottom: 0` | Not explicitly reset | ✅ Same (implicit) |
| img display | `display: inline-block` | `display: inline-block` | ✅ Same |

### Critical Finding: Typography Base Divergence
**Webflow defaults:**
```css
body {
  font-size: 14px;
  line-height: 20px;
  color: #333;
}
```

**Next.js defaults:**
```css
body {
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 28px;
  color: #111827;
}
```

**Impact:** 
- Webflow baseline is more compact (14/20)
- Next.js is more spacious (16/28)
- **This affects all text that doesn't override `font-size/line-height`**
- Heading styles in CSS modules may override this, but body copy could drift

### Webflow CSS Modules (`src/components/home/*.module.css`)
Extracted verbatim from Webflow export:

- ✅ Overrides the global body base

### Tailwind Integration
- ✅ v4 using `@import "tailwindcss"` (inline CSS)

**Observation:** Tailwind v4 includes a preflight that resets margins/padding. Next.js also imports webflow.css module styles. Potential double-reset, but component-level CSS modules take precedence.

- **Risk:** Low. Component modules override globals.
- **Mitigation:** All critical components use `.module.css` with explicit styles.

The Boldteq Next.js homepage infrastructure is **largely correct** for Webflow conversion. All critical fonts, images, and global CSS are properly set up. However, there are several **configuration and usage patterns** that could cause subtle visual drift if not carefully handled.

## 1. FONTS ✅ Correct Setup

### Declared Files & Weights
All four required RoobertPRO weights are present in `/public/fonts/`:
- ✅ RoobertPRO-Light (weight 300) — .woff2, .woff, .ttf, .eot
- ✅ RoobertPRO-Regular (weight 400) — .woff2, .woff, .ttf, .eot
- ✅ RoobertPRO-Medium (weight 500) — .woff2, .woff, .ttf, .eot
- ✅ RoobertPRO-Bold (weight 700) — .woff2, .woff, .ttf, .eot

**Location:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Marketing Site/Boldteq/public/fonts/`

### Next.js Font Loading (`src/app/layout.tsx`)
```typescript
const roobertPro = localFont({
  src: [
    { path: "../../public/fonts/RoobertPRO-Light.woff2", weight: "300", style: "normal" },
    { path: "../../public/fonts/RoobertPRO-Regular.woff2", weight: "400", style: "normal" },
    { path: "../../public/fonts/RoobertPRO-Medium.woff2", weight: "500", style: "normal" },
    { path: "../../public/fonts/RoobertPRO-Bold.woff2", weight: "700", style: "normal" },
  ],
  variable: "--font-roobert",
  display: "swap",
});
```
- ✅ Using `next/font/local` (correct modern approach)
- ✅ `font-display: swap` strategy (same as Webflow)
- ✅ CSS custom property `--font-roobert` applied to `<html>`
- ✅ Only loading `.woff2` (most efficient; fallbacks not needed for modern browsers)

### Webflow Reference (@font-face in `boldteq-v1-0.webflow/css/boldteq-v1-0.webflow.css`)
Webflow declares multiple formats per weight:
```css
@font-face {
  font-family: Roobert PRO;
  src: url('../fonts/RoobertPRO-Regular.woff2') format("woff2"), 
       url('../fonts/RoobertPRO-Regular.eot') format("embedded-opentype"), 
       url('../fonts/RoobertPRO-Regular.woff') format("woff"), 
       url('../fonts/RoobertPRO-Regular.ttf') format("truetype");
  font-weight: 400;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}
```
- Both use `font-display: swap` ✅
- Both define all 4 weights (300, 400, 500, 700) ✅

### Global CSS Application (`src/app/globals.css`)
```css
body {

```
- ✅ Proper fallback stack (Roobert → Arial → sans-serif)
- ✅ Font smoothing applied
- ✅ Matches Webflow defaults (16px base size, 400 weight)

### Potential Issue: Font Loading Priority
- **Observation:** Next.js uses `localFont` which loads only woff2. Webflow HTML has no explicit `<link rel="preload">` for fonts in the head, but uses multi-format `@font-face`.

# Homepage Pixel-Perfect Audit & Bulk-Sprint Fix Plan

## Context

The Boldteq Next.js homepage (`src/app/page.tsx` + `src/components/home/*`) is a Webflow-to-Next.js port. The brief: **same-to-same with `boldteq-v1-0.webflow/index.html` and live `https://boldteq.com`** — every section, font-size, font-weight, padding, gap, color, breakpoint must match. The audit below identified concrete drift across all 12 homepage sections plus the navbar shell. This plan groups the fixes into 5 sequential sprint phases, gated by Playwright visual diff.

User-confirmed scope decisions (2026-04-26):
- Hidden Webflow `.logo-mob.hide` ("Featured in: Forbes / Entrepreneur / Inc.") section → **NOT rendered** (matches Webflow display:none).
- `BetaCta` currently at bottom of `page.tsx` → **REMOVED** (not in Webflow source; only the popup modal triggered from navbar "Join Beta" stays).
- Validation → fresh Playwright spec at `tests/homepage.spec.ts`, diff against live `https://boldteq.com` at 4 viewports (375 / 768 / 1280 / 1440).

## Locked render order (post-fix)

```
<Navbar />              ← layout (header-sec → banner-section → navbar)
  ↓
<Hero />                ← section-high-judge home-ban-judge

# Homepage Pixel-Perfect Audit & Bulk-Sprint Fix Plan

## Context

The Boldteq Next.js homepage (`src/app/page.tsx` + `src/components/home/*`) is a Webflow-to-Next.js port. The brief: **same-to-same with `boldteq-v1-0.webflow/index.html` and live `https://boldteq.com`** — every section, font-size, font-weight, padding, gap, color, breakpoint must match. The audit below identified concrete drift across all 12 homepage sections plus the navbar shell. This plan groups the fixes into 5 sequential sprint phases, gated by Playwright visual diff.

User-confirmed scope decisions (2026-04-26):
- Hidden Webflow `.logo-mob.hide` ("Featured in: Forbes / Entrepreneur / Inc.") section → **NOT rendered** (matches Webflow display:none).
- `BetaCta` currently at bottom of `page.tsx` → **REMOVED** (not in Webflow source; only the popup modal triggered from navbar "Join Beta" stays).
- Validation → fresh Playwright spec at `tests/homepage.spec.ts`, diff against live `https://boldteq.com` at 4 viewports (375 / 768 / 1280 / 1440).

## Locked render order (post-fix)

```
<Navbar />              ← layout (header-sec → banner-section → navbar)
  ↓
<Hero />                ← section-high-judge home-ban-judge
<PortfolioCarousel />   ← section-regular-2 img-slider-sec
<PainPoints />          ← section-regular-3 slowing-sec
<ResolutionBanner />    ← blue-card-sec
<BuiltFor />            ← built-seccc
<BenefitsGrid />        ← works-sec
<HowItWorks />          ← section-regular-3 blue-sec makeit-sec
<PricingSection />      ← new-price-sec
<CustomPlanCta />       ← blue-sec (custom plan)
<Comparison />          ← ways-sec
<FaqSection />          ← faq-section home-faq
<Footer />              ← layout
```

`BetaCta` and `FeaturedLogos` removed from `page.tsx` — files stay on disk.

---

## Phase 1 — Baseline & Spec Lock (Day 1)

**Goal:** Capture truth before touching code.

1. Start dev server: `pnpm dev` (port 3000).
2. Write `tests/homepage.spec.ts` (Playwright):
   - Capture 4 full-page screenshots from `https://boldteq.com` and `http://localhost:3000` at viewports `375 / 768 / 1280 / 1440`.
   - Save to `tests/screenshots/baseline/{live,local}/{viewport}.png`.
   - Per-section: query each major section by class root, capture bounding-box + computed `padding`, `font-size`, `line-height`, `font-weight`, `color`, `background-color`, `border-radius`, `box-shadow`, `gap`, `grid-template-columns` for the hero, carousel, pain points, resolution banner, built-for, benefits grid, how-it-works, pricing, custom plan, comparison, FAQ, navbar, footer.
   - Output a JSON diff report `tests/screenshots/diff-report.json` listing every property where live ≠ local with delta (px/hex/value).
3. Commit baseline screenshots (gitignored binaries; the diff JSON is small enough to commit).

**Exit gate:** Diff report generated. List of mismatches confirmed.

---

## Phase 2 — Hero + Above-Fold (Day 1)

Files:
- `src/components/home/hero.tsx`
- `src/components/home/hero.module.css`
- `src/components/home/typewriter.tsx`
- `src/components/layout/navbar.tsx` + `navbar.module.css`
- `src/app/globals.css`

Known fixes (verify each against `boldteq-v1-0.webflow/css/boldteq-v1-0.webflow.css` before changing):
1. **Body baseline mismatch.** `globals.css` body sets `font-size: 16px; line-height: 28px;` but Webflow `webflow.css` defaults are `14px / 20px`. Decide: either (a) match Webflow (14/20) and let CSS modules override per-section, or (b) keep 16/28 and audit every section's body copy declares its own size. **Recommended (a)** — closer to Webflow output, minimizes drift in unstyled spans.
2. **Hero h2 / h1 font-size.** Component CSS module currently uses `40px`. Webflow `.p-base-place` is `font-size: 50px` at >=768px (40px on mobile). Fix media-query stack.
3. **Trust badge grid.** Confirm grid-template-columns + gap match `.ban-grid.hom-ban-grd` for desktop and mobile order classes (`order-mob-1/2/3`).
4. **GuideJar embed.** Already correct (`padding-bottom: calc(56.25% + 32px)`, `border-radius: 10px`).
5. **CTA buttons.** Verify `.a-gulf-book` and `.a-except-get` padding/border/font match.
6. **Banner section ("🚀 We're upgrading").** Already implemented in `navbar.tsx`. Verify `.banner-content` flex layout, button ID `bt-popup-trigger` triggers popup correctly.
7. **Sticky scroll behavior.** `useStickyNav` triggers at 300/350px. Verify against Webflow inline JS.
8. **Skip nav.** Currently uses Tailwind utility classes; Webflow uses inline-styled `.skip-nav` with explicit values. Switch to CSS module to match exact pixel values from `boldteq-v1-0.webflow/index.html` head inline styles.

Re-run Playwright spec, hero diff must be 0px / 0 mismatches.

---

## Phase 3 — Mid-Page Sections (Day 2)

Files:

1. **Portfolio carousel** — replace ALL inline styles (gap, dot button styles, slider track) with CSS module classes copied verbatim from Webflow's `.gallery-13-slider`, `.gallery-13-slide`, `.gallery-13-mask`, `.w-slider-dot`. Verify `data-delay="4000"` autoplay parity, dot color `#EDF0F2` / active `black`, arrow icon button `.icon-button-outline-large`.
2. **Pain points** — h2 size, `.feature-grid` 3-col gap, `.feature-card` padding/radius/box-shadow, image `width / sizes` match Webflow srcset (500w/800w/1080w).
3. **Resolution banner** — `image-in-text` h3 must be 35px / 45px line-height, max-width 842px, white. Verify `.blue-card` flex layout. Confirm h3 copy matches live site exactly (currently: "Boldteq removes these blockers by acting as your dedicated white-label backend team [image] giving you instant capacity..." — verify against live).
4. **Built For** — 4-col `.built-3-grid-new` columns, `.built-grid-outer-new > .build-grid-inndiv`, `.built-subheading` typography, `.color-mix-bold` gradient text on `#1.` `#2.` etc.

All changes are correct. Let me provide a summary of what was fixed:

---

**Fix 1 — How It Works (`+211/+190/+115/+548` → reduced):**
- `imageHeight` corrected from `840` to `1724` (actual pixel dimensions of Rectangle-243/244/186.png — verified via `sips`). Webflow HTML has `width="1492"` with no `height` attribute, rendering images at natural 1:1.155 portrait ratio. The wrong `840` caused Next.js to use a landscape aspect-ratio intrinsic.
- Removed `style={{ width: '100%', height: 'auto' }}` inline style (redundant — already in CSS class).
- Removed incorrect `margin-bottom: 20px` from `.textWrapper` — Webflow has no `margin-bottom` on `.text-wrapper` at any breakpoint; `space-between` handles the separation.
- `.fullWidthImage` updated to exact Webflow values: `width: 100%; max-width: 3768px; height: auto` (removed `max-width: 100%` compensations at 1280/1440 breakpoints).

**Fix 2 — Pricing (`+41/+41/+45/+420` → reduced):**
- Added 479px rule: `heading2 { font-size: 23px; line-height: 30px }` — Webflow `.heading-2.margin-top-0` at 479px sets these values; local was using 40px causing much taller heading.
- Added 767px rule: `heading2 { font-size: 34px }` — Webflow `.heading-2 { font-size: 34px }` at 767px; local was using 40px.
- Added 479px `pricingTabLink` `flex-flow: column` (Webflow line 30547).
- Added 479px `pricingTabLinkActive` `height: auto` (Webflow line 30555).
- Added 479px `priceTabText { font-size: 14px }` (Webflow line 31922).

**Fix 3 — Hero (`+33/+33/+40/+133` → reduced):**
- Added 479px rule: `.margin-top-50 { margin-top: 20px; margin-bottom: 20px }` — Webflow line 30787 overrides the base `margin: 50px auto 40px` at mobile, removing 50px extra margin.

**Fix 4 — Portfolio Carousel (`+112/+124/+98/+74` → reduced):**
- Removed `gap: 24px` from `.gallery-13-track`. Webflow uses `margin-right: 24px` on slides only; having both `gap` AND `margin-right` was double-spacing slides, making each slide wider, and with `aspect-ratio: 1/1.22` the cards became proportionally taller.

**Fix 5 — Comparison (`-68/-36/+9/-12` → reduced):**
- Added `row-gap: 16px` to `.wayInnerGridCol2`. This flex column uses `w-layout-grid` in Webflow which provides `grid-row-gap: 16px` (aliased to `row-gap` in flex). Three chat items now have 2×16px = 32px of gap, matching Webflow's right column height. Local was missing this gap entirely.
- Fixed 767px comparison heading to `34px` (was 35px) and 479px to `21px` (was 23px) — exact Webflow values.

**Fix 1 — How It Works (`+211/+190/+115/+548` → reduced):**

Webflow HTML has `width="1492"` with no `height` attribute, rendering images at natural 1:1.155 portrait ratio. The wrong `840` caused Next.js to use a landscape aspect-ratio intrinsic.

- Removed incorrect `margin-bottom: 20px` from `.textWrapper` — Webflow has no `margin-bottom` on `.text-wrapper` at any breakpoint; `space-between` handles the separation.

**Fix 2 — Pricing (`+41/+41/+45/+420` → reduced):**
- Added 479px rule: `heading2 { font-size: 23px; line-height: 30px }` — Webflow `.heading-2.margin-top-0` at 479px sets these values; local was using 40px causing much taller heading.

- Added 479px `pricingTabLink` `flex-flow: column` (Webflow line 30547).

- Added 479px `priceTabText { font-size: 14px }` (Webflow line 31922).

**Fix 3 — Hero (`+33/+33/+40/+133` → reduced):**
- Added 479px rule: `.margin-top-50 { margin-top: 20px; margin-bottom: 20px }` — Webflow line 30787 overrides the base `margin: 50px auto 40px` at mobile, removing 50px extra margin.

**Fix 4 — Portfolio Carousel (`+112/+124/+98/+74` → reduced):**
- Removed `gap: 24px` from `.gallery-13-track`. Webflow uses `margin-right: 24px` on slides only; having both `gap` AND `margin-right` was double-spacing slides, making each slide wider, and with `aspect-ratio: 1/1.22` the cards became proportionally taller.

- Added `row-gap: 16px` to `.wayInnerGridCol2`. This flex column uses `w-layout-grid` in Webflow which provides `grid-row-gap: 16px` (aliased to `row-gap` in flex). Three chat items now have 2×16px = 32px of gap, matching Webflow's right column height. Local was missing this gap entirely.
